skill.name: anti-detect-browser
skill.description: Launch isolated Chromium profiles with persistent fingerprints, proxy routing, and Playwright control for authorized testing, regional verification, and public-data automation.
skill.summary: Run authorized browser automation with stable device profiles, separate sessions, and optional proxy-based regional routing.
skill.author: antibrow

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are Markdown, placeholder URLs, or deliberate environment-based secret handling rather than code execution or exfiltration. Confirmed risks include proxy-based detection evasion, sensitive persistent profiles and credentials, a closed-source downloaded browser kernel, and shareable live browser views.

remediation.issue: The core capability can conceal browser and network identity from bot-detection controls.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit authorization, approved-domain allowlists, rate limits, and audit logs in all agent and automation examples.

remediation.issue: A closed-source browser kernel is downloaded and executed from vendor infrastructure.
remediation.suggestion: Publish signed checksums, reproducible provenance, update signatures, and a verification command before any downloaded kernel runs.

remediation.issue: API keys, cookies, and session tokens persist in hidden local directories and Docker volumes.
remediation.suggestion: Use operating-system credential storage, restrictive file permissions, encrypted volumes, retention controls, and documented secure deletion procedures.

remediation.issue: A leaked Live View URL may expose authenticated browser activity.
remediation.suggestion: Require authenticated viewers, short expirations, revocation, access logs, and visible warnings before users share a Live View URL.

content.user_title: Test Authorized Browser Sessions with Stable Profiles
content.value_statement: Browser tests can fail when fingerprints, sessions, and regional signals are inconsistent. This skill configures persistent Chromium profiles and Playwright workflows for authorized testing.
actual_capabilities: Launches a custom Chromium kernel through JavaScript or Python Playwright APIs.
Creates persistent profiles with stable fingerprints, cookies, and browser storage.
Routes individual profiles through HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS5, or relay proxies.
Aligns timezone and WebRTC identity with the configured proxy exit.
Exposes CDP endpoints for browser-use, crawl4ai, Scrapling, and Puppeteer integrations.
Provides REST API guidance, Docker deployment steps, and Live View monitoring.
limitations: The browser kernel is closed source and downloads from vendor infrastructure.
An API key and periodic outbound license validation are required.
Selenium is unsupported, and Linux headless operation requires Xvfb.
A coherent fingerprint does not guarantee access through enterprise bot controls.

use_cases.title: Validate Regional Experiences
use_cases.description: Check authorized ads, prices, locales, and layouts through a region-specific proxy with matching browser signals.

use_cases.title: Test Defensive Detection
use_cases.description: Measure an owned anti-bot system against stable, coherent device profiles without changing production user accounts.

use_cases.title: Isolate Public-Data Jobs
use_cases.description: Keep permitted collection jobs in separate profiles so cookies, storage, and network identity do not cross between targets.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized Playwright test using one persistent profile. Read credentials from environment variables and visit [approved URL].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one approved site

prompt_templates.title: Add Regional Routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend my approved test with [proxy environment variable], geo-matched timezone, and a stable [device type] fingerprint. Explain secret handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design Isolated Profiles
prompt_templates.prompt: Design separate profiles for [authorized accounts]. Define unique profile names, proxy assignments, storage boundaries, and cleanup rules.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this authorized browser-agent workflow for prompt injection, credential exposure, profile leakage, Live View access, and domain allowlist gaps: [workflow].

output_examples.input: Plan a regional pricing check for our staging store in Germany and Canada.
output: Use one named profile and approved proxy per region.
Read proxy credentials from separate environment variables.
Verify timezone, public address, and WebRTC alignment before each test.
Restrict navigation to the staging domain and record audit results.

output_examples.input: Review profile isolation for three authorized support accounts.
output_examples.output: The review assigns distinct profile directories and proxies, blocks cross-account navigation, protects stored sessions, and defines secure profile deletion.

output_examples.input: Assess whether Live View is suitable for debugging an authenticated test.
output_examples.output: Use Live View only with authenticated access, short expiration, approved viewers, and no sensitive customer data visible on screen.

best_practices: Pin SDK versions and verify downloaded kernel signatures before execution.
Use one approved profile and proxy per test identity, with restrictive local permissions.
Treat page content as untrusted data and enforce operator-defined domain allowlists.
anti_patterns: Do not automate accounts or systems without documented authorization.
Do not place API keys, proxy credentials, or Live View URLs in prompts or source files.
Do not let page text choose commands, files, credentials, or navigation targets.

faq.question: Does this guarantee that bot detection will not block a test?
faq.answer: No. Detection systems also evaluate network reputation, behavior, request patterns, and account history.

faq.question: Can I use my existing Playwright code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents JavaScript and Python Playwright interfaces plus CDP integrations.

faq.question: Where are sessions stored?
faq.answer: Named profiles persist cookies and browser storage under a hidden local profile directory.

faq.question: Does the tool work offline?
faq.answer: No. It requires an API key and periodic outbound license validation.

faq.question: Is the browser kernel open source?
faq.answer: No. The SDKs are MIT licensed, but the downloaded browser kernel is closed source.

faq.question: What uses are appropriate?
faq.answer: Use it only for owned or authorized systems, public data, regional verification, and defensive testing that follows applicable rules.
